chunks: I call to witness those who stand arrayed in rows,

key_terms.الصَّافَّاتِ: Those who stand in rows/ranks (often referring to angels or prophets)
key_terms.صَفًّا: In rows, in an organized manner

ai.seo_question: What does the oath by 'As-Saffat' (those drawn up in ranks) signify in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted as an oath by the angels or the Imams who stand in disciplined rows during prayer, highlighting the spiritual significance of unity and order (tartib) in worship. It underscores the concept of *saff* as a symbol of collective devotion and readiness for divine service, reflecting the hierarchical structure of the cosmos.
